official.deadline_central_display: 15 January (close of the first admissions round)
official.deadline_note: Malmö University publishes no separate calendar date for the scholarship itself; it is granted only to applicants admitted in the first admissions round, which for autumn 2027 runs 16 October to 15 January. Supporting documents are due 1 February, master's results are published 1 April, scholarship offers go out by the end of April, and the tuition fee payment deadline is 10 May.
official.application_cycle: Autumn 2027 intake - first admissions round 16 October 2026 to 15 January 2027
official.status_note: The first admissions round for autumn semester 2027 opens 16 October and closes 15 January. Only students admitted to their first-choice programme in that round are considered, and admitted students are then told how to apply for the scholarship after the Notification of Selection Results.
official.tuition_coverage_note: They cover partial or up to the full tuition fee but do not cover other expenses, such as living expenses.

official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is aimed at non-EU/EEA, non-Swiss fee-paying master students. EU/EEA and Swiss applicants are exempt from application and tuition fees and therefore are not the target group; citizens of EU/EEA countries and Switzerland may also apply in the second admissions round for autumn 2027.

official.description: Malmö University states that each year it offers a limited number of scholarships to qualified master students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are required to pay tuition fees, awarded on the basis of academic merit, experience and motivation.
official.program_type: University tuition-fee scholarship for master students
official.english_requirement: Programmes are English-taught; English language requirements are set through University Admissions and the individual programme's entry requirements.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition-only award: it can wipe out your fee bill in full but leaves your rent, food and travel entirely to you, so never treat an offer as a living-cost solution. Eligibility collapses into one mechanic - Malmö must be ranked as first choice at University Admissions and you must apply in the first round, because the second round exists only for EU/EEA and Swiss citizens. Because only a handful of awards are made each year and unsuccessful applicants are not told, build a parallel plan for paying the first tuition instalment, which is due 10 May.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A fee-paying non-EU/EEA master applicant whose first choice is genuinely a Malmö programme and who can point to both academic results and a CV showing social engagement.
application_readiness_checklist: Rank Malmö University as choice 1 of 4 at universityadmissions.se before the 15 January close of the first round
Pay the SEK 900 application fee - an unpaid fee stalls the whole application
Upload all supporting documents, including the Bachelor's Degree Certificate, by 1 February
Prepare a CV that evidences social engagement, since that is an explicit selection criterion alongside grades
Plan the tuition payment route before results land on 1 April, in case the scholarship does not come through
common_rejection_risks: Ranking Malmö second or lower, which removes you from contention outright
Applying in the second admissions round, which is closed to non-EU/EEA citizens
Assuming the scholarship has its own deadline and missing the admissions round that actually gates it
Treating the award as full funding and then being unable to show living expenses for the residence permit
Losing the second year of a two-year programme by dropping below 22.5 credits in a semester or 45 credits across the year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Malmö, flights, insurance beyond what Swedish student arrangements cover, and the first tuition instalment if an award is not granted in time. Full tuition for two-year programmes ranges from roughly SEK 220,000 to 395,000 depending on the programme, so a partial waiver can still leave a substantial balance.
document_audit: Non-Swedish degree documents must follow the country-specific instructions on universityadmissions.se, and an incorrect document set is treated as a late or incomplete application
The Bachelor's Degree Certificate must be uploaded for master's study even if you are in your final year - a conditional admission based on a pending degree can collapse into a refund request
Documents must be uploaded to the national portal, not emailed to Malmö, and the deadline is 1 February rather than the 15 January application close
alerts: Only a few students receive the scholarship each year and non-recipients are never notified, so silence is not a signal to wait on
The tuition payment deadline is 10 May, and a full scholarship triggers a refund of fees already paid - the SEK 7,000 administrative deduction is waived only in that case
Second-year retention is conditional on hitting 45 credits across the academic year, so a slow first semester directly risks the funding
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: First-round application with fee at universityadmissions.se, documents by 1 February, master's results 1 April, scholarship instructions sent to admitted students, offer by end of April, tuition payment by 10 May.
